completion_data.completion_summary: Completed Phase 6: migrated 25 test suites (the 7 test-lint-*.sh suites from the Phase 3/5 cluster plus 18 of the smallest remaining core suites) onto common.sh's test harness (common_test_pass/_fail/_info, common_test_repo_root, common_test_resolve_candidate, common_test_workdir_init), deleting each suite's own hand-rolled boilerplate. 23 of 25 suites' output is byte-identical before/after; 2 carry cosmetic-only diffs (an [INFO] prefix standardization and a dropped ANSI color wrap) with identical assertion counts and PASS/FAIL case names. Two migration-script defects (a brace-interpolation deletion bug, a case-arm/single-line call-site rename miss) were caught by the mandated before/after diff and fixed before closing. NET-TEST -355 for this phase, confirmed via both script-inventory.sh --size-line and git diff --numstat. file_scope for this task was missing the 18 non-lint suite paths; appended them and landed a follow-up commit for the files the phase-commit wrapper's containment check had dropped.

memory_candidates.content: When mechanically renaming bare shell function call sites (e.g. pass()/fail()/info() -> common_test_pass/_fail/_info) across a batch of files via regex, a line-start-anchored pattern ('^[ \t]*name "') reliably misses call sites inside case-statement arms ('pattern) name "msg" ;;') and single-line 'if ...; then name "msg"; fi' shapes. If the local function definition is deleted first, an unrenamed call silently falls through to any same-named binary on PATH (observed: the real UNIX 'pass' password-store tool), producing a runtime error message rather than a syntax error, and silently drops the suite's reported assertion count. bash -n does not catch this -- only an actual before/after run with output diffed against a captured baseline does. Prefer a word-boundary rename anywhere on the line (\bname(\s+")) over a line-start anchor, and always diff full captured stdout/stderr before and after a batch rename, never just exit code.

A regex that deletes a one-line shell function definition using a '[^\n}]*' body-match (stopping at the first literal close-brace) breaks on a definition containing a brace-interpolation like ${VAR} or ${VAR:-default} on the same line, since the interpolation's own closing brace satisfies the stop-class early and leaves a dangling fragment of the original line in the output -- a bash syntax error, but only caught by actually running `bash -n`, not by eyeballing the diff. When deleting single-line function definitions across a heterogeneous batch of files, either match the full statement list up to the FINAL unmatched closing brace, or verify every edited file with a syntax check immediately after the batch transform and before any behavioral diff.

A task's declared file_scope in specs/state.json is descriptive/anticipated, not filesystem-validated, and a phase whose own plan text says a file list will be 'enumerated at implementation time' (rather than pre-named) will routinely touch files outside the scope recorded at task-creation time. git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check drops any files_touched path not contained by file_scope (drop-and-warn, never blocking), including, in the observed case, files nested under a directory entry already listed in file_scope with a trailing slash -- the containment check did not treat that directory entry as covering its descendants. The sanctioned recovery is to append (never wholesale-replace) the missing concrete paths to file_scope, then land a scoped follow-up commit of exactly the dropped paths via git-commit-scoped.sh -- never widen the original commit's pathspec and never skip updating file_scope, since the next phase's commit would drop the same files again.
